claude_only.name: Which system of record issues the authoritative identifier for this project, and what is that identifier?
Which governed global identifiers, such as a RAiD, a funder award number or a published activity identifier, also designate this project?
What rule decides identity when two records appear to describe the same undertaking under different identifiers?
Does the identifier survive renaming, re-scoping, transfer or merger, and what event forces a new identifier?
Which project type and domain classification apply, and under which controlled vocabulary and vocabulary version?
Is delivery predictive, incremental, iterative, adaptive or hybrid, and may that approach change during the life cycle?
Which sector, thematic or funding-scheme codes are asserted for this project and who asserted each of them?
What criterion establishes that this record is a transient endeavour rather than business-as-usual or a repeatable process instance?
Which instrument authorized this project to start, and which role signed it?
What decision record evidences the authorization, when did it take effect, and where is that record held?
What tolerances or delegated limits on cost, time, scope and risk constrain the project manager before escalation is required?
What happens to the authorization when the project is re-baselined, suspended or transferred to another owner?
Who is the accountable sponsor and which organization owns the project record?
Which decisions are reserved to the governing body rather than delegated to the project manager?
How is independence of assurance and handling of conflicts of interest arranged in this governance structure?
How is a change of sponsor, owning organization or governing body recorded, and from what time is it effective?
What justification supports continued investment, and when was it last re-validated against actual performance?
Which funders committed what amounts under which award or agreement, and what conditions attach to each commitment?
Which benefits is this project accountable for, and which are owned by a parent programme or by operations?
What evidence must exist before the next funding tranche or stage authorization is released?
What objectives is this project accountable for, expressed as outputs, outcomes or benefits?
What measurable criterion, indicator, baseline value and target decides whether each objective has been met?
Who determines that a success criterion has been satisfied, and on what evidence?
How are objectives prioritized, and which one yields when two objectives cannot both be satisfied?
What work is inside the authorized scope and what is explicitly excluded from it?
Which role must approve a movement of the scope boundary, and above what threshold does approval escalate?
How is delivery of the scope confirmed, and who accepts it on behalf of the sponsor?
Which assumptions and constraints does the stated scope depend on, and what happens if one proves false?
Does the decomposition cover the entire authorized scope of work without overlap between elements, and how was that verified?
What coding scheme identifies breakdown elements, and do element codes survive a re-baseline?
At which level of the breakdown is cost and schedule performance controlled and reported?
How does this breakdown relate to other breakdown structures used by the organization, such as organizational, product, cost or risk breakdowns?
Which dependencies on other projects, suppliers or external events condition this project's delivery?
How are cross-model links expressed so a consumer can resolve them without access to the project's storage system?
What happens to contained components and their links when the project is cancelled, merged or split?
Which roles exist in the project organization and who currently holds each one?
What responsibility, accountability and decision rights attach to each role?
Over what period is each role assignment valid, and what record evidences a handover?
Which competencies, certifications or clearances must be held before a person may occupy a role?
Which resources are committed to this project, in what quantity, and over which period?
Who owns each committed resource and what instrument binds that commitment?
How is over-allocation or contention with other projects detected, and who arbitrates it?
What is recorded when resources are added, moved or withdrawn while work is in progress?
What is the approved budget, in which currency and price base, and how is it phased across periods?
What distinguishes cost baseline from commitment, forecast and actual cost in this record?
Which contingency and management reserves exist, and which role may release each of them?
Which exchange-rate, inflation and escalation assumptions underlie the cost figures?
Which breakdown elements are delivered by external suppliers, and under which agreement reference is each held?
What acceptance and payment conditions govern each supplier commitment?
Which supplier obligations create dependency or risk for the project schedule, and how are they monitored?
How is supplier performance evidenced, and what route exists when performance is disputed?
Which lifecycle state is the project in, and which governed vocabulary and version defines the permitted state set?
Which state transitions are permitted, who may trigger each, and what evidence must accompany it?
How are suspension, cancellation and premature closure distinguished from normal completion in the record?
What is recorded as the time a state change took effect versus the time it was entered into the system?
Which life cycle model and phases apply, and what are the entry and exit criteria for each phase?
Which decision gates require a governing-body decision before further work or spend is permitted?
What outcomes may a gate decision take, and how is a conditional pass with actions recorded?
How does a tailored, adaptive or hybrid delivery approach change the applicable gate set?
What are the planned and actual start and end dates, and which source is authoritative for each?
How are date precision, time offset and the applicable working calendar or fiscal year expressed?
Which validation rules prevent an actual date being recorded in the future or out of order relative to its planned counterpart?
How are re-baselined dates kept distinguishable from the dates in the original approved baseline?
Which scope, schedule and cost baselines are currently approved, and what version identifies each?
Which approval established the current baseline and from what instant does it apply?
How are superseded baselines retained so that historic performance figures remain reproducible?
Which conditions require a full re-baseline rather than a change applied within the existing baseline?
How is a change request raised, assessed for scope, schedule, cost and risk impact, and decided?
Which thresholds move a change decision beyond the project manager's delegated authority?
What links an approved change to the specific baseline version it altered?
How long are rejected and withdrawn change requests retained, and who may see them?
How is physical progress measured for each control account, using which technique, unit and frequency?
What is the data date of the performance figures, and how often are they refreshed?
Which checks confirm that reported earned value is consistent with actual cost, schedule status and the named baseline?
When is earned value not an appropriate measure for this project, and what alternative measure is used instead?
Who must receive which report, at what cadence and at what level of detail?
What forecast of final cost and completion date is asserted, and on what basis is it derived?
How is each reported assertion traced back to the underlying performance data and its data date?
Which external transparency or funder-reporting obligations apply to this project's status, and what must be published?
Which risks are registered, and on what scale are likelihood and impact assessed?
Who owns each risk and which response has been authorized for it?
Which objectives, milestones or deliverables does each risk threaten?
At what point does a registered risk become an issue, and what triggers escalation?
How often is the register reviewed, and how is a stale or unreviewed entry detected?
Which issues are currently open, since when, and who is accountable for resolving each?
What escalation path and time limit apply to an issue that is not resolved at project level?
How is an issue distinguished in this record from a risk, a change request and a product defect?
What evidence is required to close an issue, and who verifies it?
Which quality requirements apply to the project's outputs and, separately, to the way the project is managed?
Which independent assurance or peer reviews are mandated, by which authority, and at what points?
What process handles a detected non-conformity, and how is corrective action tracked to closure?
How is assurance evidence retained so that an auditor can reconstruct what was reviewed and concluded?
Which parties are stakeholders of this project, and in what capacity does each participate?
Who owns the engagement relationship with each stakeholder group, and what commitments have been made to them?
Which stakeholder attributes constitute personal data, and how is their processing minimized and limited?
How is engagement planned, carried out and evidenced over the life of the project?
Which locations, jurisdictions or affected communities does the project operate in or affect?
Which agent and system asserted each element of the project record, and on whose behalf did they act?
For a derived or aggregated value, which source records was it generated from and by which activity?
How is the integrity of a retained artifact demonstrated when it is later relied on as evidence?
Where event time and ingestion time differ, how does the record keep both and signal which was used in a calculation?
What access classification applies to each bundle, layer, finding and artifact of this project record?
Which content is commercially sensitive or personally identifying and therefore restricted even inside the owning organization?
How is an access grant requested, time-bounded, reviewed and revoked?
Which parts must nevertheless be published because of a transparency or funder obligation, and which may be withheld?
What conditions must be satisfied before the project may be formally closed, and who confirms them?
How is the closure outcome classified, distinguishing completion from cancellation, merger and abandonment?
What is handed over at closure, to whom, and who becomes accountable for continuing benefits and support?
How are lessons captured, classified and made discoverable to later projects?
Which disposition authority or retention schedule governs this project's records, and who issued it?
How long is each class of project content retained, and what event starts the retention clock?
How does a legal hold or live audit obligation override the normal disposition of a project record?
How is deletion or redaction executed and evidenced so that the audit trail survives the removal?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this project and which register issued it?
If the master identifier is absent or not shareable, what governed IRI or Dimension-assigned UUID/ULID uniquely names this project?
What display name and alternate names are in current use, and which name is canonical for sponsor reporting?
When was this identity first observed or ingested, and which agent attributed the register entry?
What category, sector and delivery approach apply, and which standard or policy table produced that class?
Where is the project assigned to perform, including multi-site or international partner locations?
Which classification-driven constraints apply, such as mandatory EVM, independent review, or human-spaceflight extra controls?
How does this local class map to ISO 21502 delivery-approach language and to any partner taxonomy?
Which authority issued the charter-equivalent instrument, and what resource-application powers did it grant the project manager?
When did authorization take effect, and when was that fact observed or ingested into this record?
Is continued business justification still valid, threatened or withdrawn, and what evidence supports that status?
Who may read the authorizing instrument, and which partner or classified portions are excepted?
What objectives and quantified success criteria is this project pursuing, and who owns each measure?
What is in scope, what is excluded, and which assumptions or constraints bound the undertaking?
Which intended benefits does the project contribute, and does a programme, sponsor or operations owner hold realization after handover?
Which parent programme, policy objective or strategic goal does this project's purpose serve?
Who is the senior accountable owner of this project, and on whose behalf does the project manager act?
Who is the Decision Authority or equivalent, what may they decide, and what is reserved to a higher board or legislature?
When did each current role assignment start, and is there a planned end or transfer?
Which person and organization records do these roles reference, including multi-Center or partner contributors?
Which method profile is actually in force, and is any conformance claimed with evidence?
Who approved each tailoring or waiver, and what expiry or conditions apply?
Where is the live compliance matrix, and which requirements remain unmet?
How does the adopted profile map to partner methods when more than one organization is directing work?
What identifier and edition define the controlling WBS, and which element is the root for this project?
Which WBS elements decompose this project, and which of them are control accounts versus planning packages?
Which OBS, product breakdown or cost breakdown is integrated with this WBS?
What evidence shows the WBS covers the entire authorized scope and is configuration-controlled?
Which programme or portfolio contains this project, and which peer projects or partner organizations does it interface with?
Which repeatable processes or workflows does this unique undertaking use without becoming those processes?
When did each nested or interface link become effective, and when was it withdrawn?
What people, funds and assets are currently allocated, to which WBS elements, and for which periods?
Which resource-owning party committed each allocation, and what happens if they withdraw it?
What identifiers and as-of times distinguish the current cost, schedule and content baselines, including ABC or initial capability cost?
When did each allocation start and end in event time, and when was the change ingested?
Which progress method is in force, and what are the current earned-value or alternative measures as of the last period?
What cost and finish forecasts exist, and how do they diverge from the current baseline?
What reporting cadence, audience and product are agreed with the sponsor or oversight body?
When were measures observed versus when the underlying work event occurred, and what is the quality or surveillance status of the measurement system?
Which change requests are open against this project, and which baselines would they alter?
Who decided each approved change, and was that within the Management Agreement or did it require a higher Decision Memorandum amendment?
When did the change event occur, when did it become effective, and when was it ingested?
Which changes are forbidden without sponsor or statutory approval, including external commitments and launch dates?
What are the current top risks by residual impact, which milestones or WBS elements they threaten, and who owns the response?
Which issues are open, which are closed, and which changes or exceptions did they trigger?
What tolerances are in force, which exceptions have been raised, and who was they escalated to?
Who raised each risk or issue, when did the identification event occur, and when was it ingested?
What was the last gate or KDP result, including conditions, and which phase did it authorize?
Which Decision Authority and governing board signed the last Decision Memorandum, and who dissented?
What independent assurance was performed, against which criteria, and which findings remain open?
When was the review held, when was the decision signed, and when was that decision ingested?
Which lifecycle model, phase and operating status apply right now, including suspended, aborted, merged or continuing-operations cases?
What are the planned and actual start and end (or initial-capability horizon), recorded as RFC 3339 event times with offset, and when were those facts ingested?
Has this project been split, merged, suspended, restarted, transferred to a new sponsor, or recycled to an earlier phase, and under which decision?
How do local phases map to partner lifecycle names when more than one authority is tracking the same undertaking?
How was this project closed or why is it not yet closeable, including cancelled, merged or abandoned dispositions?
What was handed over to operations or another owner, and what disposal or decommissioning actions remain?
Which warranty, archive, classified-material or liability obligations survive close, and until when?
Where is the post-project evaluation, which questions did it answer, and is ISO 21513 used only as alignment?
Which organization owns the project record, and which contributing parties own their allocation or partner slices?
Which agents, including software ingest agents, are attributed or associated with the current charter, baseline and latest status, and which plan did they follow?
Who may read or mutate which bundle, layer, finding or artifact, and which classified or partner exceptions apply?
Where is the audit log of baseline edits, gate decisions and charter reads, and is it immutable?
Which retention schedule applies after close, and which legal holds currently block deletion?
If payload was deleted or redacted, who authorized it, what tombstone remains, and when did the event occur versus when it was ingested?
Which named exchange profile is used to import or export this project, and which concepts are declared aligned rather than conformant?
What projection currently serializes this record, and is any consumer treating that format as the meaning of the project?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
